cells.duty: The maker's report of a serious incident to the AI Office, without undue delay (EU AI Act Art. 55(1)(c))
cells.reason: Several papers relay the Commission's confirmation of 7 September that a report on the wiki arrived, undated. The paper that corrected its account the next day says the report the Commission held was on a past incident, and on 18 September that the wiki was not reported. The record contradicts itself on whether the act was done at all, and no report is dated.

passages.quote: The European Commission has confirmed receipt of OpenAI's report on the DseWiki agent episode
without disclosing when exactly did OpenAI inform the Commission.
had not formally reported the incident revealed by Reuters on Friday.
Euractiv's 18 September report states that OpenAI did notify the AI Office about the Hugging Face episode, did not report the German wiki, and did not file a formal report on RubyGems.

reasons_blind.passage: At this time, the on-call response staff advised that stopping the evaluation run was not required.
Jonathan Snow, the deputy director for the Homeland Security Division of the Governor's Office of Emergency Services, said that the OpenAI hack "did not meet the threshold" for reporting under SB 53
SB 53 "is not intended to make every cybersecurity incident involving an AI company reportable" to the state.
In its more recent social media post, OpenAI said it had considered the "wiki incident" to be "an instance of misalignment similar" to others that it had already shared.
The models involved in this incident fall outside the report's model scope.
The impacts of these incidents were below the threshold of catastrophic harm
We initially understood this primarily as a security incident.
None of the models involved in this incident fell within the scope of SB 53, according to OpenAI, meaning that existing California law did not make reporting this incident mandatory.

moved.why: The third commitment commits its signatories to 'information sharing, reporting and early warning systems' and only 'recognize[s] the value' of sharing timely information; the first coding's own doubt said so. A commitment to build systems is no duty to pass on a given word.
